AUDIT QUESTION: pp-selectid (Protocol Pulse clip-video builder), RULING 158 (2) (STANDING, HARD: "on-screen advertising refuses a clip in every format ... When unsure, treat it as an ad"; PBX: "we never include any sponsor material, ever"), uncommitted (diff below). The integrator's render-side vision check found a clip from a conference stage with a sponsor logo wall ("Powered by Cash App", bitkey, SALT) and holds it; this side must agree. THE CHANGE: visual_pin's vision question 5 now names sponsor material at events (a stage backdrop, banner or wall of sponsor logos, "powered by", "presented by", a row of company logos behind a speaker), and AD_WORDS (the code's own rule on every text the check copied, except the source's burned captions of the spoken words) adds "powered by", "presented by", "official sponsor/partner", "in partnership with". visual_pin.ad_block refuses on anything question 5 lists or on AD_WORDS; layout_block puts that first (every role and format). The prompt is part of the cache key (visual_pin.key digests PROMPT), so every clip is asked the new question.
CHECK, quoting the code: can a clip whose frames or copied texts show event sponsor material still pass; can an event's own name ("BITCOIN 2024 NASHVILLE") or ordinary Bitcoin words now be refused as ads by AD_WORDS; did the edit break the regex or the prompt's JSON template. Report only what the code shows.

-   listed under question 4. IF YOU ARE UNSURE whether something is an ad, LIST IT. An empty list means you saw NO
-   advertising in any frame.
+   service (open an account, an IRA, an exchange, a wallet, a card, a loan, a funding reward). SPONSOR MATERIAL TOO: a
+   stage backdrop, banner or wall of sponsor logos at an event ("powered by", "presented by", a row of company logos
+   behind a speaker). Read the small print of every box and panel at the sides and corners. Copy its text exactly and
+   name what it advertises. An item may ALSO be listed under question 4. IF YOU ARE UNSURE whether something is an ad,
+   LIST IT. An empty list means you saw NO advertising in any frame.

     r"\bpaid\s+(?:partner|partnership|promotion)\b|\b\d+\s*%\s+off\b|\bfree\s+trial\b|\bcoupon\b|"

+    r"\bofficial\s+(?:sponsor|partner)\b|\bin\s+partnership\s+with\b", re.I)   # the event sponsor walls (the
+#   integrator's V1, 02:0x ET Nov 24: a Bitcoin Magazine stage clip, "Powered by Cash App", bitkey, SALT)
 #   RULING 158 (2): offer phrases that make a copied text an ad, whatever kind the check filed it under (the Kraken
 #   banner of Nov 23 came back as a "ticker": "... KRAKEN $25 SIGN UP BONUS ..."). Never bare words that Bitcoin talk
